papers.title: The Rehabilitation Gap: Mine Closure Liabilities, Financial Assurance and the Intergenerational Economics of Responsible Extraction
papers.description: This independent research examines the discrepancy between the long-term costs of mine closure and the financial arrangements protecting communities, regulators and future generations. The paper analyses restoration, water treatment, tailings, regulatory security, accounting provisions and post-mining transitions through comparative evidence. It proposes a CLOSURE Integrity Framework as author analysis, not as a certified standard, and distinguishes dated regulatory observations from hypothetical financial scenarios.

papers.title: The Water Allocation Economy: Mining, AI Infrastructure, Hydrogen and the Next Constraint on Industrial Growth
papers.description: Dependable industrial growth requires lawful allocation of water of the right quality and quantity while preserving public services and ecosystems. This monograph studies the relationship between water, power, mining, data centres, semiconductors, hydrogen and basin governance. It introduces the author-developed BASIN Allocation Protocol, seven-ledger water accounting and governance controls. Institutional evidence, forward scenarios and analytical propositions are clearly distinguished.

papers.title: The Carbon Integrity Divide: Article 6, Industrial Carbon Accounting and the New Rules of Credible Climate Value
papers.description: A corporate greenhouse-gas inventory, carbon credit, Article 6 unit, product footprint and border-adjustment obligation are different instruments with different claims. This research reviews 2026 institutional developments in carbon markets, industrial carbon reporting and international transfers. The author proposes a Seven-Ledger Integrity Architecture and assurance controls to reconcile physical changes, legal rights, registries and public claims. The framework is original analysis rather than an external certification.

papers.title: The Chokepoint Economy: Critical Minerals, Export Controls and the New Architecture of Industrial Security
papers.description: The security of critical-mineral supply depends on more than domestic ore reserves. Processing capacity, trade restrictions, logistics, qualification and recycling affect whether material becomes available to industry. This study synthesizes institutional evidence and proposes a Source-Process-Route-Qualify-Recycle framework for assessing vulnerabilities and investment responses. It distinguishes supply-chain resilience from national mineral self-sufficiency.

papers.title: AI Assurance for Guyana's Extractive Sector: A Risk-Based Governance Blueprint for Mining, Environmental Compliance and Worker Protection
papers.description: Artificial intelligence offers applications in mining efficiency, hazard detection and environmental monitoring, but statutory accountability remains with identifiable decision makers. This paper proposes a consequence-based assurance framework for Guyana's extractive sector, covering risk classification, human oversight, data provenance, validation, explainability and incident escalation. It uses international frameworks as references while clearly separating recommendations from existing legal duties.

papers.title: Nature as National Wealth: Financing Guyana's Biodiversity through Sovereign Leadership, Indigenous Stewardship and Disciplined Global Investment
papers.description: An independent executive research paper proposing a Guyana nature-finance platform, three investment windows and safeguards for Indigenous rights, ecological measurement, financial integrity and transparent public accountability.

papers.title: Guyana's Uranium Opportunity: A Strategic Assessment of Geological Potential, Market Positioning, Development Pathways and National Value Creation
papers.description: A strategic assessment of historical uranium exploration evidence at Kurupung, mineral processing constraints, uranium-market positioning, radiation governance and responsible development pathways. The analysis distinguishes historical resource estimates from verified current mineral resources.

papers.title: Standing Forests, Measurable Outcomes: The Climate Value of Forest Protection, Governance and Carbon Accountability
papers.description: An independent evidence synthesis and audit-ready evaluation framework for forest protection, causal climate benefits, carbon stocks, counterfactual forest-loss measurement, Guyana's reference-level accounting, Indigenous rights and climate finance. Complete expanded second edition.

papers.title: The New Resource Security Order: Critical Minerals, Energy, Artificial Intelligence, Trade and the Reconfiguration of Global Power, 2026-2040
papers.description: An independent strategic analysis of the interaction among mineral processing, electricity systems, AI infrastructure, international trade, industrial policy, investment and strategic alliances through 2040. The evidence cut-off is 11 October 2026.

papers.title: Guyana Freshwater Security to 2035: From Water Abundance to Safe Supply, Functioning Watersheds, Productive Use and Climate Resilience
papers.description: A research edition assessing Guyana's freshwater resources, safe drinking-water services, public-health protection, groundwater, watershed governance, agricultural and industrial demand, water-loss scenarios and investment priorities through 2035. Evidence cut-off: 26 September 2026.
